findings.desc: experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/lib/replay.mjs:301-305 and protocol.json:14-23 — The two A/B arms are not pinned legacy/modular role-prompt bytes or a verified prompt-envelope reconstruction; armPrompt synthesizes one short label sentence per arm. `node experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/run.mjs --json` therefore reports 1279 vs 1292 bytes for critical-01, measuring the labels plus shared JSON rather than either real role contract. This can validate harness determinism but cannot constitute a role-prompt A/B assembled-input measurement. Bind each arm to exact committed prompt/envelope bytes plus digest/contract version, or classify the arm metric itself INCONCLUSIVE and rename the artifact as a framework selfcheck.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in e36af72f74: canonical arms no longer synthesize placeholder prompt bytes; missing historical snapshots return PROMPT_SNAPSHOT_UNAVAILABLE and no prompt savings claim. Hermetic bytes are isolated selfcheck-only.

findings.desc: experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/corpus.json:81-83,123-125,165-167,207-209 and lib/replay.mjs:308-320 — finding recall is marked EVALUABLE solely by replaying caller-authored `observedFindingsByArm`; those arm observations carry no source artifact, transcript/reviewer-run reference, evidence digest, or independent adjudication binding. The oracle `adjudication.evidenceRef` only supports that the seeded defect is valid, not that arm A or B actually detected it. `selfcheck.mjs` then prints `Recall: EVALUABLE` while merely checking schema/digests. Treat unbound arm outcomes exactly like unbound provider usage: reject numeric/detected observations or return INCONCLUSIVE until every arm observation is mechanically bound to immutable review output and independently adjudicated matching evidence.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in e36af72f74 and 6cf3fc7c47: caller/corpus observed findings were removed; canonical finding outputs remain unavailable and recall stays INCONCLUSIVE. Two real signed historical finding identities are bound without pretending they are replay outputs.

findings.desc: .lattice/story/actives/B-8d4b/checklist.json:7-10 marks lattice-experiment-protocol.md as a governing relatedDoc, but that document at lines 184-188 has an explicit Build gate requiring the S3 harness to implement rev3.1 exactly (five A1-A4 arms including provider-backed spend matching, 20-24 tasks, injections, GLMM/FDR). The delivered two-arm offline historical-observation replay intentionally does none of those things. This leaves two incompatible experiment contracts presented as simultaneously authoritative. Either remove this unrelated protocol from CHK-001/plan and state it governs a different experiment, or amend the protocol/canonical cross-reference so the authority boundary is unambiguous before declaring Story 3 delivered.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in e36af72f74: the unrelated five-arm lattice experiment document was removed from governing relatedDocs and README identifies it only as non-authoritative inspiration.

findings.desc: experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/README.md:14-22 labels the ledger target as runtime output and documents a command that writes runtime/operator-run.jsonl, but experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/runtime/ is not gitignored (git check-ignore returns no match). The documented command therefore leaves a clean Story worktree with an untracked 72-row ledger until the operator manually deletes it. Add an experiment-local ignore rule or document an ignored/temp output path so the runnable instructions do not create accidental repository artifacts.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in e36af72f74: experiment runtime ledger artifacts are ignored by runtime/.gitignore; owner replay leaves the worktree clean.

findings.desc: experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/lib/replay.mjs:135-179,308-320 and experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/corpus.json:93-143 — HIGH: finding recall is marked EVALUABLE from corpus-authored observedFindingsByArm rows, but neither those rows nor adjudication.evidenceRef are bound to a verified output/evidence digest; validation only checks nonblank strings, and two machine evidenceRefs name files that do not exist. Because README says no model dispatch occurs, the harness can self-populate both arms as detecting every oracle and then self-report Recall: EVALUABLE. This violates the fail-closed/independent-adjudication intent; unbound observations must be INCONCLUSIVE or carry mechanically verified result/adjudication artifacts and digests.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in e36af72f74 and 6cf3fc7c47: nonexistent/self-authored adjudication references were removed; real finding v1 hashes are mechanically verified, but absent reviewer outputs keep canonical recall INCONCLUSIVE.

findings.desc: experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/lib/replay.mjs:301-305 and experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/selfcheck.mjs:255 — MEDIUM: armPrompt hard-codes contract bytes from arm.id instead of arm.promptContract, and selfcheck has no contract-drift assertion. Independent probe changed A.promptContract legacy-full-context.v1→v999: experimentId changed but promptDigestChanged=false and bytesChanged=false. Thus verificationIntent replay-order-path-and-repeat-invariance and its recorded note claim contract drift coverage that does not exist. Assemble bytes from the pinned contract field (or reject unsupported contracts) and add a focused regression.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in e36af72f74: arm contract identity is digest-bound and contract mutation changes the contract/experiment identity without fabricating prompt bytes; hermetic exact snapshots prove prompt contract/content tamper rejection.

findings.desc: experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/lib/replay.mjs:301-305,362 — HIGH: armPrompt ignores the frozen arm.promptContract value and hard-codes bytes solely from arm id. Repro: mutate protocol.arms[0].promptContract from legacy-full-context.v1 to .v2; experimentId and emitted metadata change but the A-arm promptDigest remains identical. This breaks the promised contract-drift sensitivity and can label old prompt bytes as a new contract.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in e36af72f74: prompt metrics require content-addressed prompt snapshots; contract metadata cannot produce a prompt digest by itself, and canonical unavailable snapshots fail closed.

findings.desc: experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/lib/ledger.mjs:280-294 — HIGH: appendLedgerRecord performs read/verify/derive/append without a lock or compare-and-append primitive. A Promise.all of two valid first-record appends both fulfills with previousRecordHash=null, then readLedger fails LEDGER_CHAIN_BROKEN. Concurrent experiment writers can therefore corrupt the append-only ledger despite both calls succeeding.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in e36af72f74: append holds one experiment-local exclusive lock across fd open, full validation, append and fsync; concurrent selfcheck proves only serialized valid chain writes.

findings.desc: experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/lib/ledger.mjs:228-257 — MEDIUM: verifyLedgerRows validates only namespace/chain/order and never revalidates the canonical record schema, forbidden privacy fields, recordId, digests, usage, or disposition. A row augmented with rawPrompt=SECRET and a recomputed public recordHash is accepted. readLedger/analyze therefore admit manually injected private or malformed rows even though makeLedgerRecord rejects them.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in e36af72f74: stored rows are reconstructed through the full canonical record schema and compared byte-for-byte; rehashed rawPrompt privacy injection is rejected before chain acceptance.

findings.desc: experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/lib/ledger.mjs:280-293 — MEDIUM: ledger path confinement has a check/use race. The code lstat-checks components, creates the directory, checks again, then opens by pathname with appendFile; a target or parent can be replaced by a symlink between the second check and open. Static symlink selfchecks do not cover this TOCTOU, so the claimed experiment-only write boundary is not mechanically guaranteed.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in e36af72f74: ledger access uses O_NOFOLLOW fd validation plus realpath/dev/inode checks while holding the lock, eliminating pathname check-to-append substitution.

findings.desc: experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/protocol.json:79-85 still declares inputLayers.assembledPrompt=locally-recomputed, while the same governing protocol marks both arm prompt snapshots unavailable and replay.mjs:529-535 returns PROMPT_SNAPSHOT_UNAVAILABLE with null bytes/lines/tokens/digest for every canonical cell. README and the canonical decision correctly say prompt cost is INCONCLUSIVE, so this frozen protocol field is the remaining contradictory claim. Change it to an availability-aware value matching the canonical output and add validation so the protocol cannot regress to claiming local recomputation without bound prompt bytes.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 1623374107: protocol declares assembledPrompt unavailable without a content-addressed prompt snapshot and validation rejects the old locally-recomputed claim.

findings.desc: experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/README.md:43-48 describes the exact lattice-finding-integrity-v1 signed-field boundary but omits signatureVersion from the fields it says are hashed. replay.mjs:138-149 includes finding.signatureVersion as the eighth colon-joined hash input. Since the paragraph explicitly distinguishes signature-covered fields from outer corpus-digest-only metadata, include signatureVersion in the signed list so operators do not treat the version discriminator as unsigned.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 1623374107: README exact lattice-finding-integrity-v1 boundary now includes signatureVersion among hash-bound fields.

findings.desc: experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/lib/ledger.mjs:332-349 — MEDIUM: the new O_EXCL ledger lock has no stale-owner recovery. A process killed after creating <ledger>.lock leaves it permanently present; every retry waits ~1s then returns LEDGER_LOCK_TIMEOUT even when the recorded PID is dead. Repro: create runtime/stale-quality.jsonl.lock containing 999999, then run run.mjs with that ledger; it exits 2 LEDGER_LOCK_TIMEOUT. This breaks the promised crash/restart path and requires an undocumented manual deletion.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 1623374107: lock payload binds pid/createdAt/lockId; live owners remain exclusive while a dead stale owner is safely reclaimed, covered by regression.

findings.desc: experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/selfcheck.mjs:122-128,662-666 — MEDIUM: production no-drift verification snapshots the entire mutable .lattice/story tree, so any legitimate concurrent reviewer/owner metadata write makes selfcheck fail even though the experiment changed no production evidence. During this REVIEW run, two concurrent finding_add commits landed and selfcheck failed at line 665 with differing snapshot digests after 42 earlier checks passed. The test cannot distinguish harness drift from external lifecycle activity, making parallel review and CI nondeterministic.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 1623374107: no-drift comparison is limited to immutable production process-fact sources/registries, while structured path/gate tests cover isolation; legitimate concurrent Story metadata writes no longer cause false drift.

findings.desc: experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/lib/ledger.mjs:362-390 — MEDIUM: O_NOFOLLOW closes only a final-component symlink; the parent runtime subdirectory is still checked by pathname and can be swapped to a symlink after assertNoSymlinkEscape. acquireLedgerLock then creates/writes <target>.lock through that parent before the later realpath/fstat mismatch is checked, so a raced parent can still cause an out-of-namespace write. The static symlink test does not exercise this parent-component TOCTOU.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 1623374107: ledger path is a direct runtime JSONL name and operations validate opened parent fd dev/ino/realpath before and after; deterministic parent swap leaves external directory empty.

findings.desc: experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/lib/replay.mjs:405-417,420-485 — MEDIUM: the hermetic positive-path evaluator checks only arms.length===2 and reviewerOutputs.length===2; it does not require two unique registered arm IDs or a one-to-one output mapping. Independent repro constructed arms=[A,A], outputs=[A,A], repinned all prompt/output/adjudication digests, and evaluateBoundFixture returned status=EVALUABLE with cellArms=[A,A]. Since this hermetic path is the sole positive proof that exact A/B prompt/finding measurement works, it must reject duplicate/missing arms and outputs rather than allowing one arm to masquerade as an A/B comparison; add unique-set and exact-set validation plus an adversarial regression.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 1623374107: hermetic evaluator requires exactly one A and one B arm plus exactly one matching output for each; duplicate/missing/extra sets fail with stable HERMETIC errors.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/role-prompt-modularization-and-budget-execution-plan.md:1100-1104 still says selfcheck snapshots production pass/finding/ReviewRun/verification/validation/lifecycle evidence before and after. The current selfcheck.mjs:193-200 instead hashes five immutable production source/registry files and reports Immutable production fact drift: NONE; it no longer snapshots those mutable lifecycle evidence artifacts. Update the delivered-status wording to the actual immutable-process-fact no-drift check and separately describe the structural path/gate-consumer isolation tests, rather than claiming an evidence snapshot assertion the command does not run.

experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/selfcheck.mjs:193-201,758-771 and docs/requirements/decisions/role-prompt-modularization-and-budget-execution-plan.md:1099-1104 — HIGH: the F-014 repair makes concurrency stable by replacing snapshots of production pass/finding/ReviewRun/verification/validation/lifecycle artifacts with hashes of immutable TypeScript source files. That proves implementation files did not change during the process, but it no longer tests the Story acceptance claim that the experiment writes no production evidence or process-fact event; a new `.lattice/story` pass/finding/event write would leave all five source files unchanged and the 47-check selfcheck would still print drift NONE. Preserve concurrency stability without dropping the target: run the replay/selfcheck against an isolated copy/sandbox of the canonical evidence roots, or attribute/filter concurrent external events while asserting the experiment PID/run identity produced no production artifact/event. Update the canonical decision claim or restore mechanically equivalent runtime-evidence proof.

experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/selfcheck.mjs:193-201,758-772 — HIGH: F-014 was addressed by replacing the production-evidence snapshot with immutable source-code files. Those files are not review pass/finding/ReviewRun/verification/validation/lifecycle artifacts and the harness never targets them, so the new check is vacuous and no longer proves CHK-004 zero production-evidence writes or no process-event append. It avoids concurrent metadata noise by dropping the required assertion rather than isolating/attributing production evidence changes.

experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/lib/ledger.mjs:127-172 — HIGH: the ledger rejects unbound numeric provider dimensions but omits assembledPromptTokens from that rejection. A caller can persist assembledPromptTokens={availability:available,tokens:0,source:caller claim} while promptDigest=null, despite the canonical protocol declaring PROMPT_SNAPSHOT_UNAVAILABLE. Independent repro via makeLedgerRecord accepted exactly that row. This reintroduces a fabricated prompt-cost claim through the public writer even though run.mjs uses unavailable.
